mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met, or the effect reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the relationship inverts during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong export demand.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a fall in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.5% in the same month signals a disinflationary tightening, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls > 0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the effect is not statistically significant at p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and a fall in housing starts (HOUST) signals a shift from durable goods consumption to residential investment, which historically precedes equity market weakness due to lower cyclicals outperformance and lower growth expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises AND HOUST falls in the same month
regime_hint: transition from consumption-led to investment-led growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered months compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% for six consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, prompting preemptive monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during periods of stable inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above trend for three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS above trend for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher during triggered periods compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.10).
